title: Q4 Coordination Plan: Hosted Endpoints & Model Fleet Prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a prioritized, operationally-ready plan for the hosted endpoint fleet and model variants to execute during Q4. Goal is to align product, engineering, ML Ops, and sales on which models to promote, downgrade, or deprecate across hosted tiers to hit cost, latency, and quality goals. Scope includes model scoring rubric, rollout windows, canary policy, customer communication templates, and handoff docs for Dedicated/Private teams.
background: Over the last two quarters we added multiple community model variants and automatic quantized builds. This increased catalog breadth but raised unit-cost variance and made SLO guarantees harder to reason about. We need a deliberate prioritization approach for Q4 so that roadmap work (autoscaling, kernel selection improvements, and console UX updates) can be targeted to the highest-impact models and endpoints.
objectives: Create a reproducible model scoring rubric (latency/cost/quality/stability) to rank catalog items for hosted endpoints
Reduce average per-token cost for the hosted standard tier by at least 15% vs. Q3 baseline without degrading core quality metrics
Define and schedule canary windows and rollback playbooks for top-20 hosted endpoints
Publish customer-facing change plan and API contract for announced deprecations with 60-day notice
Ensure Dedicated and Private teams have migration playbooks for any deprecated hosted variants
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented and validated with 3 sample models; rubric stored in Confluence with version tag
Top-20 model list prioritized and assigned owners for follow-up work
Canary schedule committed to calendar with window owners and testing checklist
Cost projection model showing >=15% reduction for hosted standard tier across expected traffic profile
Customer communication templates and support runbook reviewed by Customer Success
Migration playbooks for Dedicated/Private accepted by those teams and linked in the playbook
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Insufficient eval workloads to surface real-world regressions — Mitigation: partner with three active customers for closed evals and synthetic traffic that mirrors heavy tails
Risk: Model deprecations trigger support load — Mitigation: early comms, concierge migrations for top customers, and feature flags for temporary compatibility
Risk: Kernel/quantization changes introduce perf regressions — Mitigation: require benchmark harness gating and per-model rollback plan
stakeholders: Eng Leads: Daniel Kim (Serving Runtime), Priya Shah (Infra)
